playGuides.title: Calling for ability checks
playGuides.intro: Call for a roll only when the outcome is uncertain and both success and failure are interesting. Say the ability (and skill) and the DC (or at least 'easy', 'hard') before the dice land.

tips.text: No roll when there is no time pressure and no cost to retrying: the character simply succeeds, given enough time.
Failure moves the story too. Let them succeed at a cost, learn something partial, or lose time, rather than ending the scene.
Use passive scores (10 + bonus) for things the characters notice without trying, so players are not asked to roll Perception every room.
Advantage and disadvantage are your quickest dial: give advantage for a good plan or help, disadvantage for bad footing or darkness.
Group checks keep a party moving together: if at least half succeed, the group succeeds.
Skills are a lens on an ability. When a different ability fits the fiction better, pair them: Strength (Intimidation) for a show of force.

groups.label: Strength
groups.summary: Raw force: lifting, shoving, breaking, holding on.

groups.label: Constitution
groups.summary: Endurance: pushing on, holding breath, keeping food down.

entries.label: Strength check
entries.summary: Raw force: lifting, shoving, breaking, holding on.
callFor: a door is barred and time is short
someone tries to wrestle an object away
the bridge ropes snap and a hero has to hold the weight
entries.success: The obstacle gives way, loudly. Ask what they do with the opening.
entries.failure: It holds, and the effort costs something: noise, time, or a dropped torch.
examples: Make a Strength check to force the portcullis up.

entries.label: Dexterity check
entries.summary: Balance, nimble hands, quick reactions.
callFor: a ledge is narrow and the wind is up
a hand slips into a pocket in a crowd
a falling chandelier gives a heartbeat of warning
entries.success: Smooth and quiet; they are where they wanted to be.
entries.failure: They make it, but not cleanly: a stumble, a scrape, or someone noticed.
examples: Roll Dexterity to catch the vial before it shatters.

entries.label: Constitution check
entries.summary: Endurance: pushing on, holding breath, keeping food down.
callFor: a forced march goes past nightfall
the swamp air is foul
a drinking contest decides who gets the map
entries.success: They keep going; the cost lands on someone or something else.
entries.failure: They pay in time, a level of exhaustion if the rules call for it, or a lost advantage.
examples: Constitution check: can you keep pace through the night?

entries.label: Intelligence check
entries.summary: Recall, reasoning and deduction.
callFor: a clue only makes sense with the right knowledge
a mechanism has a logic to it
two accounts of the same night disagree
entries.success: Give a real, specific fact or connection, not a vague hint.
entries.failure: They still learn something, but it is incomplete or comes with a wrong assumption.
examples: Make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to work out how the lock resets.

entries.label: Wisdom check
entries.summary: Awareness, intuition and judgment.
callFor: something is watching from the dark
a merchant's smile does not reach the eyes
the trail goes cold
entries.success: Tell them what they notice and what it probably means.
entries.failure: They notice it too late, or read it wrong; the world acts first.
examples: Wisdom (Perception): what do you see in the treeline?

entries.label: Charisma check
entries.summary: Presence: persuading, deceiving, performing, intimidating.
callFor: a guard can be talked past
a crowd needs to be turned
a noble has to believe a lie
entries.success: The other side moves, within reason: they agree, hesitate, or reveal something.
entries.failure: They refuse, raise the price, or remember the face. Never a dead end: offer another way.
examples: Roll Charisma (Persuasion) to get the captain to delay the hanging.

entries.label: Acrobatics
entries.summary: Staying upright and moving with flair.
callFor: ice, rigging or a rolling deck
a tumble past a foe
landing from a fall without fuss
entries.success: They land on their feet with options open.
entries.failure: They go down or lose their footing; the next roll may be harder.

entries.label: Animal Handling
entries.summary: Calming, reading and guiding animals.
callFor: a panicked horse at the cliff edge
a guard dog that has not decided yet
a mount pushed past its limits
entries.success: The animal settles and cooperates for now.
entries.failure: It bolts, bites or makes noise; the scene gets messier.

entries.label: Arcana
entries.summary: Spells, magic items, planes and old sigils.
callFor: a glowing circle on the floor
a magic item's purpose
a wizard's notes in shorthand
entries.success: Name the effect or the school, and one way to deal with it.
entries.failure: They know what it is, not how it ends, or they trigger it while studying it.

entries.label: Athletics
entries.summary: Climbing, jumping, swimming, grappling.
callFor: a sheer wall with a deadline
a river in flood
holding a foe down
entries.success: They get there fast and fresh.
entries.failure: They get there late or tired, or drop something on the way.

entries.label: Deception
entries.summary: Lies, disguises and misdirection.
callFor: a forged letter at the gate
bluffing a hand of cards
pretending to belong
entries.success: The lie holds, for now. Decide what would break it.
entries.failure: Doubt creeps in: questions, a follow-up, a watcher sent after them.

entries.label: History
entries.summary: Past events, wars, families and ruins.
callFor: a ruined keep's coat of arms
an old treaty
a legend that may be true
entries.success: Give a true and useful piece of the past.
entries.failure: They recall the popular version, which is wrong in one important way.

entries.label: Insight
entries.summary: Reading intentions and lies.
callFor: a too-generous offer
a nervous witness
an ally acting strangely
entries.success: Tell them what the other person wants or fears.
entries.failure: They read the mood but not the reason; they may trust the wrong person.

entries.label: Intimidation
entries.summary: Threats, menace and pressure.
callFor: a thug needs to back down
an informant is holding out
a standoff before blades are drawn
entries.success: They yield, now. Fear has a memory, though.
entries.failure: They call the bluff, get angry, or go for help.

entries.label: Investigation
entries.summary: Searching for clues and making deductions.
callFor: a ransacked room
a trap's trigger
a ledger with numbers that do not add up
entries.success: They find the clue and what it points to.
entries.failure: They find it, but it takes time, makes noise, or springs something.

entries.label: Medicine
entries.summary: Stabilizing the dying and diagnosing illness.
callFor: a friend at 0 hit points without a healer's kit
a strange sickness in the village
how long the body has been dead
entries.success: Stabilized, diagnosed, dated: give them a hard fact.
entries.failure: Time passes without progress; the patient's state is unclear.

entries.label: Nature
entries.summary: Terrain, plants, weather and beasts.
callFor: which berries are safe
a storm on the horizon
tracks of something big
entries.success: They know what it is and what it means for them.
entries.failure: They know the common case; this one is different.

entries.label: Perception
entries.summary: Spotting, hearing and sensing.
callFor: an ambush on the road
a whisper in the next room
a secret door
entries.success: They see it first. Hand them the initiative of the moment.
entries.failure: They miss it, or see it as it happens. Use passive Perception to avoid asking too often.

entries.label: Performance
entries.summary: Music, acting, storytelling.
callFor: earning a meal at the inn
distracting a crowd
a festival contest
entries.success: The audience is theirs: coin, attention, or a new admirer.
entries.failure: Polite silence, a heckler, or a rival who now wants to compete.

entries.label: Persuasion
entries.summary: Honest appeals, tact and good will.
callFor: asking a favour
negotiating a reward
calming an angry mob
entries.success: They get what they asked for, or a fair counter-offer.
entries.failure: No, not yet: a condition, a price, or a task first.

entries.label: Religion
entries.summary: Gods, rites, holy symbols and cults.
callFor: an unfamiliar altar
a cult's hand sign
an undead's weakness
entries.success: Name the faith, its customs, or what the rite is for.
entries.failure: They know the faith but miss that this is a heresy of it.

entries.label: Sleight of Hand
entries.summary: Palming, pickpocketing, planting.
callFor: lifting a key from a belt
hiding a dagger at the feast
swapping a gem for paste
entries.success: Done, and nobody saw.
entries.failure: Done, but someone saw; or not done, and nobody saw yet.

entries.label: Stealth
entries.summary: Moving unseen and unheard.
callFor: slipping past sentries
following someone through a market
an ambush of their own
entries.success: They are where they want to be and unnoticed.
entries.failure: They are spotted at the worst moment, or must pick: retreat or go loud.

entries.label: Survival
entries.summary: Tracking, foraging, navigating, enduring.
callFor: the trail splits
food is running out
a blizzard closes in
entries.success: They find the way, the food, or the shelter.
entries.failure: They lose time or supplies, or arrive somewhere unexpected.

entries.label: Strength save
entries.summary: Resisting force that would move, pin or crush them.
callFor: a wave sweeps the deck
a vine drags them toward the pit
a giant's shove at the cliff edge
entries.success: They hold their ground, and the danger turns to someone or something else.
entries.failure: They are moved, pinned or knocked down; show where they end up.

entries.label: Dexterity save
entries.summary: Getting out of the way: blasts, traps, falling things.
callFor: a fireball blooms
the floor tile clicks
rocks come down in the mine
entries.success: They dive clear, usually for half the harm; describe the near miss.
entries.failure: It catches them full on; describe the scorch, the bruise, the dust.

entries.label: Constitution save
entries.summary: Enduring poison, disease, cold and exhaustion, and holding concentration.
callFor: a poisoned blade bites
a night in the freezing pass
a caster is hit while holding a spell
entries.success: They shrug it off, for now. Concentration holds.
entries.failure: The poison takes hold or the spell drops; make the cost visible at once.

entries.label: Intelligence save
entries.summary: Seeing through illusions and resisting attacks on the mind's reasoning.
callFor: a wall that might not be there
a psychic assault
a maze that rearranges itself
entries.success: They see the trick for what it is; tell them what is real.
entries.failure: The illusion holds for them; play it straight and let the others notice.

entries.label: Wisdom save
entries.summary: Resisting charm, fear and control of the will.
callFor: a vampire's gaze
a dragon's frightful presence
a voice that offers exactly what they want
entries.success: Their will is their own; the creature knows they resisted.
entries.failure: They are charmed, frightened or compelled; give the player a clear rule for what that means.

entries.label: Charisma save
entries.summary: Holding on to their self: banishment, possession, planar pull.
callFor: a spirit tries to take over
a banishing word
a curse that would rewrite them
entries.success: They stay themselves and stay here.
entries.failure: They are pushed out of body or plane for a while; keep the player involved with what they see.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.prompt: The pitch: what kind of adventures these are (dungeon delves, a sprawling war, intrigue in one city) and why the party is together.

sections.title: The world
sections.prompt: Your world in a few paragraphs: the land where play begins, who rules it, what magic and the gods are like, and what has gone wrong lately.

sections.title: What everyone knows
sections.prompt: Legends, recent wars, rumours from the road and anything a commoner would know. Keep the secrets for play.

sections.title: Places and factions you've heard of
sections.prompt: Towns, roads, ruins and the guilds, orders and powers the characters know by name, one line each.

sections.title: House rules
sections.prompt: Critical hits, resting, encumbrance, flanking, potions as a bonus action: anything you play differently from the rules as written.

sections.title: Making your character
sections.prompt: Starting level, how ability scores are made, which races, classes, backgrounds and feats are allowed, and how the party knows each other.
sections.starter:
- **Ability scores**: standard array, point buy or rolled (say which)
- **Allowed options**: the SRD's races, classes and backgrounds, plus any supplements listed here
- **Advancement**: experience or milestones
- **Bring**: a reason to adventure and a tie to one other character

sections.title: Where we begin
sections.prompt: Where the party is when the first session starts, and the trouble that brings them together.

conditions.name: Blinded
conditions.summary: Can't see, and automatically fails any ability check that needs sight. Attack rolls against it have advantage; its own attack rolls have disadvantage.
manual: automatic failure of checks that need sight

conditions.name: Charmed
conditions.summary: Can't attack the charmer or target it with harmful abilities or magic. The charmer has advantage on ability checks to interact socially with it.
manual: can't attack or harm the charmer
the charmer's advantage on social checks

conditions.name: Deafened
conditions.summary: Can't hear, and automatically fails any ability check that needs hearing.
manual: automatic failure of checks that need hearing

conditions.name: Exhaustion
conditions.summary: Six levels, each adding to the ones below: 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws; 4 hit point maximum halved; 5 speed 0; 6 death. A long rest with food and drink lowers it by 1.

levels.summary: Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws

manual: lowering it after a long rest

conditions.name: Frightened
conditions.summary: Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of its fear is in sight; can't willingly move closer to the source.
manual: only while the source is in line of sight
can't move closer to the source

conditions.name: Grappled
conditions.summary: Speed 0, and it can't benefit from bonuses to speed. Ends if the grappler is incapacitated or it is moved out of the grappler's reach.
manual: ends when the grappler is incapacitated or out of reach

conditions.name: Invisible
conditions.summary: Impossible to see without magic or a special sense (heavily obscured for hiding), though noise and tracks can give it away. Attack rolls against it have disadvantage; its attack rolls have advantage.
manual: hiding and being located by noise or tracks

conditions.name: Paralyzed
conditions.summary: Incapacitated; can't move or speak. Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and a hit from within 5 feet is a critical hit.

conditions.name: Petrified
conditions.summary: Turned to stone with what it wears and carries: incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of its surroundings. Attack rolls against it have advantage; it fails Strength and Dexterity saves, resists all damage and is immune to poison and disease.

conditions.name: Poisoned
conditions.summary: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

conditions.name: Prone
conditions.summary: Can only crawl until it stands up, which ends the condition. Disadvantage on its attack rolls. Attack rolls against it have advantage from within 5 feet, disadvantage from farther away.

conditions.name: Restrained
conditions.summary: Speed 0. Attack rolls against it have advantage; its attack rolls have disadvantage; disadvantage on Dexterity saves.

conditions.name: Stunned
conditions.summary: Incapacitated, can't move, and can speak only falteringly. Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves. Attack rolls against it have advantage.

conditions.name: Unconscious
conditions.summary: Incapacitated, can't move or speak, unaware of its surroundings; drops what it holds and falls prone. Automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saves. Attack rolls against it have advantage, and a hit from within 5 feet is a critical hit.

zeroHp.text: A character at 0 hit points falls unconscious and makes a death saving throw at the start of each of its turns (the death save tracker): 10 or higher is a success, three successes stabilize it, three failures kill it, a natural 20 brings it back with 1 hit point. Damage at 0 hit points is a failed death save (two on a critical hit), and damage that leaves the rest equal to its hit point maximum kills it outright. Any healing wakes it.
zeroHp.cite: SRD 5.1 — Combat: Damage and Healing, Dropping to 0 Hit Points

zeroHp.text: Most monsters die at 0 hit points; an attacker who brings one down with a melee attack can knock it out instead.
zeroHp.cite: SRD 5.1 — Combat: Damage and Healing, Dropping to 0 Hit Points

blocks.title: Advantage and disadvantage
blocks.text: Roll two d20s: **advantage** keeps the higher, **disadvantage** the lower. Several sources still give only one extra d20, and having both cancels them out: roll one d20.

blocks.title: Actions
blocks.text:
- **Attack:** a melee or ranged attack.
- **Cast a Spell:** casting time of 1 action.
- **Dash:** extra movement equal to your speed.
- **Disengage:** no opportunity attacks against you this turn.
- **Dodge:** attacks against you have disadvantage; Dexterity saves with advantage.
- **Help:** an ally gets advantage on its next check, or its next attack on a foe within 5 feet of you.
- **Hide:** a Dexterity (Stealth) check.
- **Ready:** choose a trigger and an action; take it as your reaction.
- **Search:** a Perception or Investigation check.
- **Use an Object:** a second object, or one that takes an action.

You gain the following benefits.

**Two Cantrips.** You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

**Level 1 Spell.** Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat's cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have.

**Spell Change.** Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list.

steps.title: Edition
steps.intro: Which rules the character's origin follows.
guide: SRD 5.1 (2014): your race gives ability score increases; backgrounds give skills, languages and equipment.
SRD 5.2 (2024): your background gives +2/+1 or +1/+1/+1 among three abilities and an origin feat; species give traits, not increases.
Classes follow the SRD 5.1 tables either way: the SRD 5.2 classes are not in this module.

options.name: SRD 5.1 (2014 rules)

options.name: SRD 5.2 (2024 rules)
options.summary: Species, backgrounds with ability scores and an origin feat, SRD 5.2 subclasses and feats.

options.name: Mixed

mapGenerators.name: Dungeon
mapGenerators.description: An original dungeon on a 5-foot grid: a crypt, cave, keep, sewer, ruined temple or mine of one to three levels, with doors, locks, secret doors, portcullises and collapses, room purposes and dressing, encounters from the pack's encounter tables (SRD monsters), the SRD's sample traps scaled for the party, and treasure from the SRD's magic items. Accept it to add the dungeon, its rooms, encounters and monsters to the campaign.

siteTypes.label: Crypt or tomb
siteTypes.description: A processional passage with tombs in mirrored pairs, an antechamber at its foot and the burial chamber at its head.

siteTypes.label: Cave or cavern
siteTypes.description: Irregular chambers joined by winding open tunnels.

siteTypes.label: Keep, castle or tower
siteTypes.description: A rectangular block cut into rooms either side of a central hall, with a tower at each corner and the gatehouse on the front.

siteTypes.label: Sewer or aqueduct
siteTypes.description: A long water channel in sections, with chambers and side tunnels off it and an outfall at one end.

siteTypes.label: Ruined temple
siteTypes.description: A long nave with the sanctum at its head, the narthex at its foot and chapels down both sides; parts have fallen in.

siteTypes.label: Mine
siteTypes.description: Small workings strung along long, winding drifts.

var: A creature proficient with thieves' tools can pick it with a DC 15 Dexterity check.

notes.secret: Secret door: found by searching, with Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation); a medium task is DC 15, a hard one DC 20.
notes.bars: A portcullis or grate: raising or bending it is a Strength (Athletics) check.
notes.rubble: Collapsed: impassable until it is dug out.

legend.rule: Heavily obscured: a creature effectively suffers from the blinded condition when trying to see something in it. Darkvision sees darkness as dim light.

legend.rule: Every foot of movement costs 1 extra foot.

templates.name: One-shot in three acts
templates.description: A single evening: a hook that starts in motion, a middle that complicates it, and a finale with a clear win or loss.

scaffold.title: One-shot
scaffold.premise: Who needs help, what goes wrong if nobody acts, and why tonight?
scaffold.playerIntro: Start mid-scene: the characters already know each other and already have a reason to act.
scaffold.gmSituation: Write the villain's plan in three steps; each act the party fails to stop one, the next one happens.

acts.title: The hook
acts.goal: Get the party moving within ten minutes of play.
acts.pacing: One short scene of trouble, then a choice of two ways forward.

scenes.purpose: Open on trouble: an attack, a theft, a plea for help.
A quick social scene to learn what is at stake and who to trust.

acts.title: Complications
acts.goal: The obvious plan meets the villain's first step.
acts.pacing: Alternate an exploration scene with one combat; keep each under an hour.

scenes.purpose: A place to explore with a hazard or a trap and a clue to the finale.
A fight against the villain's minions; let the terrain matter.

acts.title: Finale
acts.goal: Face the villain where it matters, with the clock almost out.
acts.pacing: One big encounter with a goal besides killing everything.

scenes.purpose: The showdown, and a minute of epilogue for each character.

scaffold.epilogue: Tell each player one thing their character changed.

templates.name: Into the lair
templates.description: A location-based adventure: rumours lead to a lair, the lair pushes back, and the aftermath sets up the next session.

scaffold.title: Into the lair
scaffold.premise: Something has made its home nearby, and the people next door are paying for it.

acts.title: Rumours
acts.goal: Learn where the lair is and one thing about its master.

scenes.purpose: Witnesses disagree about what they saw.
The road there: a wilderness encounter (use the encounter generator).

acts.title: The lair
acts.goal: Get past the guardians, the hazard and the puzzle to the heart of the lair.

scenes.purpose: Entrance: a guardian or a trap that rewards caution.
A setback or a twist: an unexpected ally, prisoner or rival.
The master of the lair, on its own ground.

acts.title: Aftermath
acts.goal: Treasure, consequences and a new rumour.

scenes.purpose: Return to the people who suffered; something has changed while they were away.

scaffold.purpose: Someone has what the party needs and wants something in return.
scaffold.body:
- What do they want?
- What will they never agree to?
- What happens if the talk fails?
- Which checks fit: Insight, Persuasion, Deception, Intimidation.

scaffold.purpose: A fight with a reason and a way to end other than death.
scaffold.body:
- Why are they fighting here, now?
- Terrain: one feature that offers cover, one that is dangerous.
- When do the foes flee or surrender?
- What is the reward for winning, and the cost of losing?

items.text: Check each character's level, hit points and spell slots
items.guidance: Note who levelled up last time and who ended the session hurt or out of spells.

items.text: Pick monsters for tonight's likely fights
items.guidance: Add them from the Reference → Presets list, or roll the encounter generator; check their CR against the party's level.

items.text: Have three names and one quirk ready
items.guidance: Roll the NPC generator once or twice so improvised characters do not all sound alike.
The Initiative tracker rolls d20 plus each sheet's initiative and sorts highest first.

items.text: Note rests taken and resources left
items.guidance: Hit dice spent, spell slots used and exhaustion carry into the next session unless they rested.

items.text: Record treasure and who carries it

templates.name: Session zero
templates.description: Settle expectations before the first session; answers go into campaign settings.

items.text: What tone are we going for?
Which topics are off the table, and which should fade to black?
Starting level and how characters advance (experience or milestones)?
Which character options are allowed (SRD races and classes only, or more)?
Any house rules (critical hits, resting, encumbrance)?
Why does this party stick together?

styleNotes: Heroic fantasy: describe the world vividly, let the dice decide what is uncertain, and keep the spotlight moving between players.
SRD rules text is quoted as written; GM advice, tables and generators marked Original are Campaign Forge's own.
